summary: POST /voice/call began failing because Bolna, the outbound-voice provider, degraded. It returned 502s from about 13:19Z and then stopped answering within the 10s client timeout from about 13:41Z. fivo-api calls Bolna synchronously with no retry, so each upstream failure becomes a 502 or 504 for the caller. No deploys or config changes were recorded in the prior day, and fivo-api CPU, memory and other routes are healthy. The Bolna-side cause is not visible to us: no client-side Bolna metrics exist and traces were unavailable. Check Bolna's status page or contact them, and consider retry or a queued fallback on our side.

root_cause.component: Bolna outbound call API (POST {bolna_base_url}/call) called synchronously from app/services/bolna.py start_call, with a 10s timeout and no retry
root_cause.summary: Bolna started returning 502 Bad Gateway at about 13:19Z and then timing out at 10s from about 13:41Z. fivo-api's /voice/call handler calls Bolna inline with no retry or fallback, so each upstream failure becomes a 502 or 504 to the caller and a 'failed' voice_calls row. The 10s timeouts account for the p95 latency jump on fivo-api.

hypotheses.statement: Bolna provider degradation (5xx, then timeouts) is causing the /voice/call failures.

supporting.statement: Error logs carry upstream-originated 'bolna upstream error: 502 Bad Gateway' from 13:19:56Z, and 'bolna request timed out after 10s' with duration of about 10.01s from 13:41:02Z.
The only error groups new since baseline are /voice/call 502 and 504. The 12:00-12:30 baseline had a single /voice/call 500.
The voice_calls table records 11 failed calls with a 502 error and 11 with a timeout between 13:00 and 14:00. 23 failed and 248 queued in the 12:00-14:00 window.
The code calls Bolna synchronously inside the request with a 10s timeout, and the handler has no retry. Upstream failures therefore surface directly as 502/504.
p95 latency departs its baseline at 13:35Z and shifts to a mean of about 5.9s at 13:50Z, consistent with 10s timeouts.

contradicting.statement: There is no Bolna-side metric or status evidence, and traces were unavailable, so the upstream fault is inferred from our client-side errors only.

hypotheses.statement: A code or config change in fivo-api caused the failures.

contradicting.statement: No deploys in the 24h before the incident.
No config changes in the 24h before the incident.
The failures are all upstream-generated messages, and no other route has errors.

hypotheses.statement: Local resource exhaustion on the 512MB fivo-api instance.

contradicting.statement: Memory is flat at about 200-208 MB through the window.
Other routes stay healthy during the incident.

hypotheses.statement: Bad request data (the 422 validation errors) is behind the failures.

contradicting.statement: The 422s are fast (4ms) and are not 502/504. The 502/504 failures are upstream-generated.

facts.statement: POST /voice/call returned 202 almost exclusively until 13:10Z. 502s appear from 13:10-13:20Z, and 502 plus 504 grow through 13:30-14:00Z.
Bolna 502 errors are logged at 13:19:56Z and 13:21:55Z with durations of about 1s.
From 13:41Z Bolna calls time out at the 10s limit and return 504.
The Bolna timeout setting is 10.0s by default (BOLNA_TIMEOUT_S).
Failed calls are persisted with the upstream error text.
No deploys or config changes are recorded for the 24h before the incident.

assumptions: The 502s are returned by Bolna or its gateway, not by a local proxy. The message text says upstream, but we have no Bolna-side confirmation.
The Bolna degradation is external and not caused by anything we send, such as payload content or rate limiting. We have no evidence of request volume or rate-limit responses from Bolna.

recommended_actions.action: Check Bolna's status page and open a support ticket with sample failing trace IDs (e.g. 1369f104b1b17402, e66a5918301db8bf).
recommended_actions.rationale: The fault is on the provider side and we cannot see it ourselves.

recommended_actions.action: Add bounded retry with backoff, and queue the call through fivo-worker so the request doesn't wait up to 10s. Consider a shorter timeout.
recommended_actions.rationale: The synchronous call with no retry turns every transient upstream fault into a user-facing 502 or 504 and holds a request for 10s.

recommended_actions.action: Re-attempt or notify for voice_calls rows with status='failed' once Bolna recovers.
recommended_actions.rationale: Failed reminder calls were never placed.

recommended_actions.action: Add client-side metrics and alerting for Bolna call outcomes and latency.
recommended_actions.rationale: No Bolna client metrics exist, so we have no direct visibility into the dependency.

missing_evidence: Traces for the period are unavailable (trace store ingest backlog), so per-call spans for Bolna could not be inspected.
No Bolna-side metrics or status data, so the cause of the provider degradation is unknown.
The log counts were partial, so the exact failure ratio was not computed. The ratio exceeded 25% in the 13:40-14:00 buckets, where there were 10 successes against 7 failures, then 11 against 6.

what_changed.what_changed: Bolna's call API began failing: 502s first, then 10s timeouts. Nothing changed in fivo-api itself.
what_changed.why_not_earlier: The fault is in an external dependency. The sync, no-retry design has been in place all along and only fails when Bolna does. The exact start of the Bolna degradation cannot be established because we have no Bolna-side data. A first 502 appeared in the 13:10-13:20 bucket.

before.statement: Before 13:10Z /voice/call returned 202 at roughly 200-460ms, with no 502 or 504 and no upstream errors.

after.statement: From about 13:19Z Bolna calls return 502, and from about 13:41Z they time out at 10s and return 504. p95 latency rises to several seconds.

changes_considered.change: fivo-api deploys in the 24h before onset
Config, env var and feature flag changes in the 24h before onset
changes_considered.reason: None recorded in the same window.
